messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] SLO breach detected — streaming p99 latency spiked above 2.1s in us-west-1 at 2026-03-15T10:02:47Z. Affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/generate. Initial symptom: sustained tail stalls and higher paging.
alice (oncall): ack. I'm looking at dashboard now. p95 ~ 320ms, p99 ~ 2.1s and rising. Any deploys in last 30m?
ben (infra): there was a config rollout 00:18 ago — prefix-hash normalization change (rollout id: r-64a2). Notified by deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: deployment r-64a2 applied to edge-proxy fleet at 2026-03-15T09:58:12Z. Canary passed internal checks.
carol (runtime): re-checking cache metrics — prefix cache hit rate dropped from 82% -> 13% around the same time. Cache miss ratio jumped, causing more paging to backend shards.
alice (oncall): that matches. Streaming stalls appear when KV cache misses + paging. Are misses concentrated on a few prefixes or widespread?
ben (infra): heatmap attached (link: https://redwood.internal/metrics/heatmap/2051234567). Top prefixes show fragmentation — many small buckets.
carol (runtime): looks like the new normalization created multiple canonical keys for the same logical prefixes. Our prefix-key entropy exploded. TTLs ok, but cardinality up ~7x.
ryan (pm): we have one paying customer on a high-SLA plan in us-west. Need quick mitigation and customer impact note.
alice (oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) roll back prefix-hash normalization (fast but needs deploy), 2) enable compatibility mode (server-side config to collapse keys to old normalization), 3) increase in-memory prefetch to absorb misses.
ben (infra): I can toggle compatibility mode at the edge via config flag: `edge.prefix.normalize_mode = legacy` — doesn't require full deploy, just config push to proxies. Will take ~4m to propagate.
carol (runtime): compatibility mode will restore hit rates for previously cached prefixes. I recommend doing that first.
alice (oncall): do it. Ben, push the config and confirm.
ben (infra): pushing now. command: `kubectl -n edge set env cm edge-config PREFIX_NORMALIZE=legacy --from-file=config.yaml` (pseudo). Pushing... :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ben (infra): done. propagation started. watch metrics.
carol (runtime): monitoring cache hit rate... now 34% -> 65% after ~90s. p99 falling to 720ms.
alice (oncall): good sign. Keep an eye on p95/p99 for next 10m. Notifying support and customer for visibility.
ryan (pm): please add a short blurb for customer support: impact, what we changed, mitigation, and ETA for full fix.
alice (oncall): Draft for support: "We experienced elevated tail latency in us-west due to a recent prefix-key normalization change that caused fragmented cache keys and low cache hit rates. We pushed a compatibility-mode config to restore legacy normalization which improved cache hit rate and reduced tail latency. We're continuing monitoring and executing a permanent fix. No data loss."
ryan (pm): good. Add ETA: permanent fix target EOD local timezone.
carol (runtime): detective notes: root cause likely in the normalization mapping step of r-64a2 — strip/trim logic changed ordering for multi-sep tokens. This created distinct hashes for semantically identical prefixes. Repro locally with test corpus: see snippet:
```
# before
normalize('User:123/ctx') -> 'user:123/ctx'
# after r-64a2
normalize('User:123/ctx') -> 'user:123' + '/ctx'  # split applied twice -> different key
```
ben (infra): we should also run a backfill compaction job to remap hot keys back to legacy buckets to avoid cold miss storms while deploy is prepared.
alice (oncall): agreed. Carol, can you create the compaction job? Keep it rate-limited.
carol (runtime): yes, I'll run a throttled compaction against top-500 prefixes. Job: `python tools/compaction.py --top 500 --rate 50/s --mode merge-to-legacy`.
carol (runtime): compaction started. ETA ~18m. Monitoring hit rate as we backfill.
ben (infra): p99 now 430ms, p95 260ms. Looks stable but still slightly elevated for a subset of routes.
alice (oncall): opening incident timeline entry. tagging follow-ups: refs: INC-2051. Adding runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefix-cache
alice (oncall): handoff in 40m to night oncall @ben. I'm going to stay for the compaction completion, then handoff.
ben (infra): noted. I'll be available for the handoff.
ryan (pm): customer message posted to shared channel. also CC legal for compliance check (no user data exposure).
deploy-bot: rollback candidate r-64a2 created (id: r-64a2-rollback). Manual deploy needed for full rollback.
carol (runtime): compaction finishing early, hit rate at 79%. p99 down to 190ms. Looks like mitigation fully effective.
alice (oncall): marking incident as mitigated. still tracking RCA and corrective deploy. Next steps: 1) patch normalization unit tests, 2) schedule canary with synthetic prefix load, 3) plan gradual rollout with monitoring guard rails.
ben (infra): I've documented the config toggle and rollback steps in the incident doc.
ryan (pm): create a customer-facing postmortem draft and share with support by EOD.
alice (oncall): handing off to @ben (oncall) at 2051234830. If anything regresses, @carol and @ben will page.
ben (infra): taking over. thanks all. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2051 status -> MITIGATED at 2026-03-15T10:07:10Z. Summary: prefix normalization change caused cache fragmentation -> low hit rates -> streaming tail latency. Mitigation applied: compatibility-mode config + hot-prefix compaction. Follow-up: deploy-level fix and improved tests.
